plate_findings.evidence: superficial and deep angiocentric lymphocytic infiltrate

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: HE histology of idiopathic perniosis showing superficial and deep angiocentric lymphocytic infiltrate, matching vocabulary finding. b: HE histology of idiopathic perniosis with lymphocytic eccrine hidradenitis; dense lymphocytic infiltrate visible, tagged to perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate with proposed term for eccrine involvement. c: HE histology of idiopathic perniosis showing perivascular infiltrate surrounding capillaries and venules with endothelial alterations and red cell extravasation. d: MXA immunohistochemistry of idiopathic perniosis showing inflammatory cell infiltrate with striking MXA expression; tagged to infiltrate with proposed term for MXA positivity not in vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Magro et al. The differing pathophysiologies that underlie COVID-19-associated perniosis and thrombotic retiform purpura: a case series.. The British journal of dermatology 2021. doi:10.1111/bjd.19415. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Light microscopic findings and myxovirus resistance protein A (MXA) expression in idiopathic perniosis. (a) In each case there is a superficial and deep angiocentric lymphocytic infiltrate [haematoxylin and eosin (HE), original magnification × 100]. (b) There is a lymphocytic eccrine hidradenitis (HE, × 200). (c) The infiltrates surround and permeate capillaries and venules in the superficial and deep dermis. There are proplastic endothelial cell alterations and focal red cell extravasation without fibrin deposition (HE, × 200). (d) In all cases there is a striking expression of MXA in the epidermis, eccrine ducts and glands, inflammatory cells and endothelium (diaminobenzidine, × 200). Each scale bar is set at 125 microns.
in_text_mentions: In each case there was a superficial and deep angiocentric lymphocytic infiltrate (Figure 4a). There was lymphocytic eccrine hidradenitis in four of the six cases (Figure 4b). The infiltrate surrounded and permeated capillaries and venules of the superficial and deep dermis (Figure 4c). Vascular fibrin deposition in reticular dermal‐based blood vessels was not seen, although there was endothelial cell swelling and red cell extravasation. in_text_mentions: 10 days was prescribed. The symptoms and signs persisted and the patient arranged to see a dermatologist, who performed a biopsy of the third digit (left foot). The dermatologist declined to prescribe further treatment until the biopsy returned. The biopsy revealed a histological diagnosis of perniosis (see Figures 1,2). On further inquiry by the dermatologist, the patient stated that the evening after her pedicure she had spent several hours walking outdoors before the aforementioned university event. She had worn open-toed shoes and the wind chill factor that evening had gone as low as 0° F.

plate_findings.evidence: lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate in the dermoepidermal interface and upper papillary/reticular dermis

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is H&E histology from perniosis-like erythema case (disease-focused title) showing lymphocytic infiltrate and interface/vascular changes consistent with perniosis histology vocabulary term. B: Panel B is H&E histology from same perniosis-like erythema case showing perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with endothelial edema/swollen endothelium, matching perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate finding.
panels.attribution_text: Campos Garcia et al. Perniosis-like erythema after SARS-CoV2 infection reactivated by vaccination with inactivated virus.. Anais brasileiros de dermatologia 2023. doi:10.1016/j.abd.2022.01.015. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Elongation of epidermal rete pegs and lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate in the dermoepidermal interface and upper papillary/reticular dermis. Vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer and apoptotic keratinocytes can be observed, in addition to extravasated red blood cells (Hematoxylin & eosin, ×100). (B) In the dermis, a small-caliber vessel with swollen endothelium, demonstrating vascular aggression. Surrounding it, lymphohistiocytic inflammatory infiltrate and extravasation of red blood cells can be observed (Hematoxylin & eosin, ×400).
in_text_mentions: generation of the basal layer, apoptotic keratinocytes, superficial and deep perivascular and periadnexal lymphohistiocytic inflammatory infiltrate, in addition to endothelial edema of small vessels (Fig. 2), findings that can be observed in drug reactions and viral infections.
